findings.title: Backup code login can bypass the password check entirely
findings.body: In `authorize()` the password is only verified when `user.password && !credentials.totpCode` (line 121). The new backup-code branch is evaluated afterwards and takes precedence over the TOTP branch whenever `credentials.backupCode` is non-empty. An attacker who posts `email` + any non-empty `totpCode` (e.g. "000000") + a valid `backupCode` therefore skips password verification completely and is logged in on the strength of the backup code alone. Backup codes are long-lived static strings that users are encouraged to download to a text file (`cal-backup-codes.txt`), so this turns a comparatively weakly-protected artefact into a full single-factor account takeover. The backup-code branch must require a successful password verification for CAL-identity users (or the password check must not be skippable by merely supplying a totpCode).

findings.title: Backup code invalidation is a non-atomic read-modify-write
findings.body: The code decrypts the whole `backupCodes` array, nulls out the used index and writes the whole array back with `prisma.user.update`. Two requests presenting the *same* backup code concurrently can both pass the `indexOf` check before either update lands, so a single backup code can be consumed more than once (defeating the "each code can be used exactly once" guarantee stated in `backup_code_instructions`). Likewise, two concurrent logins using *different* codes will each write a snapshot taken before the other's update, so one consumption is silently lost and that code becomes reusable. This needs to be done in a transaction with a conditional update (or by storing codes as individual rows / hashed values that can be deleted atomically).

findings.title: Backup codes are stored reversibly encrypted instead of hashed
findings.body: `setup.ts` stores the backup codes with `symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)` and the login path decrypts them to compare. Unlike `twoFactorSecret`, backup codes never need to be recovered in plaintext after they are shown once, so they should be hashed (e.g. bcrypt/argon2, as passwords are) and compared by hash. As written, anyone with read access to the `users` table plus the encryption key (a single env var shared across the deployment) obtains working second factors for every 2FA user, and combined with the password-bypass issue in this same function that is sufficient for account takeover.

findings.title: onEnable() is now only called from the Close button, leaving UI state stale if the dialog is dismissed
findings.body: Previously `onEnable()` fired immediately after the enable API returned 200. Now it is only invoked by the `backup-codes-close` button. If the user dismisses the dialog any other way (X button, Escape, overlay click → `onOpenChange`), 2FA is already enabled server-side but the parent never learns about it, so the two-factor switch keeps showing "off" until a page reload. Worse, `resetState()` is also skipped in that path, so `step` stays at `DisplayBackupCodes` and `backupCodes` keeps the old values: reopening the modal immediately shows the previous user's/previous run's backup codes instead of starting at the password step. Reset state and notify the parent from `onOpenChange` as well.

findings.title: Submitting an empty backup code gives the user no feedback
findings.body: The login form is rendered with `noValidate`, so the `required`/`minLength` attributes on the backup-code input are not enforced, and the zod schema only validates `email`/`password` (everything else is `passthrough`). Submitting the backup-code step with an empty field sends `backupCode: ""`, the server falls through to the TOTP branch and returns `SecondFactorRequired`, which this handler maps to `setTwoFactorRequired(true)` without setting an error message. The result is a submit that appears to do nothing. Validate the backup-code field client-side (or surface an error for `SecondFactorRequired` while in backup-code mode).

findings.title: Unvalidated request body can crash the disable endpoint
findings.body: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` assumes the field is a string; posting `{"backupCode": 1}` or `{"backupCode": []}` throws `replaceAll is not a function`, and `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` throws on any corrupt/legacy ciphertext. Both throw out of the handler and surface as an unhandled 500 (with a stack trace in logs) instead of a controlled 400. Validate the body (e.g. with zod) and wrap the decrypt/parse in a try/catch returning `ErrorCode.InternalServerError`.

findings.title: missing_backup_codes message points users to a settings page that cannot generate codes
findings.body: "No backup codes found. Please generate them in your settings." is shown to any user whose `backupCodes` column is null — which is every user who enabled 2FA before this migration, since there is no backfill. There is no UI anywhere in this PR that generates backup codes for an already-enabled 2FA account; the only way to obtain codes is to disable and re-enable 2FA. The message therefore instructs users to perform an action that does not exist. Either add a regenerate action or change the text to describe the actual recovery path.

findings.title: No test covers the security-critical backup code verification paths
findings.body: The only new coverage is the download/copy/close buttons of the backup-code dialog. The actual new logic — logging in with a backup code, rejecting an incorrect code, the single-use invalidation in `next-auth-options.ts`, and disabling 2FA with a backup code in `totp/disable.ts` — is completely untested (the PR itself notes this as a TODO). Given that these paths grant account access and mutate the stored code list, at least a happy-path login-with-backup-code test plus a replay test (same code rejected the second time) should be added before merge.

findings.title: Assertion on isChecked() always passes, FIXME left in place
findings.body: `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` asserts on the returned Promise object, which is always truthy, so this step can never fail — exactly as the newly added FIXME comment says. Since the correct form is already used in the sibling test (`[data-state="checked"]` locator) or `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()`, fix the assertion rather than documenting it; as-is the first test silently stops verifying that 2FA was actually enabled.

findings.title: tabIndex={-1} makes the password show/hide toggle keyboard-inaccessible
findings.body: Adding `tabIndex={-1}` to the reveal button removes it from the tab order for every `PasswordField` in the app, not just the 2FA modals. Keyboard-only and switch-device users can no longer toggle password visibility at all (the `sr-only` label does not help because the control cannot be focused). If the goal was to keep Enter on the password field from activating the button, note the button is already `type="button"`, so removing focusability is not needed.

findings.title: Backup-code blob URL is never revoked when the modal closes
findings.body: `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` is only revoked when a new setup run creates another URL (line 98). `resetState()` and unmounting do not revoke it, so the blob containing the plaintext backup codes stays alive for the lifetime of the document and remains fetchable from its `blob:` URL after the dialog is closed. Revoke the URL in `resetState()` and in a cleanup effect on unmount.
